correctness.rationale: PASS: Directly recovered generator identity L(sum_j s_j)=-(1-gamma)sum_j s_j on every finite periodic ring, giving conditional mean m0 exp(-lambda a), with no single-spin or thermodynamic-limit inference. The continuous Pareto renewal process has mean alpha*tau0/(alpha-1) for alpha>1; equilibrium age density is survival(a)/EW, constant below tau0 and Pareto above, with masses (alpha-1)/alpha and 1/alpha. The monotone transformation a=log(m0/m)/lambda gives the complete density and no atom. Its log density derivative in age coordinates is lambda below tau0 and lambda-alpha/a above: the cusp max exists iff lambda*tau0<alpha; at equality derivative zero at the joining point but no max. Collapsing A<tau0 generates a singular point mass p=(alpha-1)/alpha, hence TV=p; the monotone shared-age coupling is W1 optimal by mean difference and yields the formula. All parameters lambda>0, tau0>0 and m0>0 observed. The 210 finite numerical checks in verify.py corroborate, not replace, this infinite-parameter derivation.

value.rationale: PASS: The very same cutoff atom interpreted as a peak in the motivating study is replaced by a continuous shoulder in the exact observable. The existence of a finite interior mode has a nontrivial sharp parameter boundary; total variation remains macroscopic while W1 tends to zero linearly as b decreases. These two precise diagnostics characterize when the cutoff approximation is qualitatively and quantitatively misleading, providing a motivated model correction rather than a routine normalization test.

final_claim: For the conditional spin-noise expectation of spatial magnetization after Pareto resets with alpha>1, the equilibrium age-change-of-variable law is atomless with the displayed piecewise density; it has a finite cutoff cusp maximum iff b=(1-tanh(2beta J))*tau0<alpha. Collapsing ages A<tau0 to tau0 changes total variation by (alpha-1)/alpha and W1 by m0(alpha-1)/alpha*((1-exp(-b))/b-exp(-b)), exactly.
limitations: Only stationary conditional mean of the finite-ring magnetization, not its sampled spin-noise distribution.
Only alpha>1, tau0>0, finite beta J and nonzero positive m0; finite-time relaxation and two-dimensional models not covered.
General renewal formula is established; originality and value are confined to this model-specific comparison and modal correction.
